title: Handler Order
statement: Implement `solve(raised, handlers)`. `handlers` is a list of exception names from the first except clause to the last. `raised` is the type that was raised. A handler matches when it equals `raised` or when it is a listed base of `raised`. The bases you must honor are: `FileNotFoundError` is a `OSError`, and `OSError` is an `Exception`. Return the first matching handler name. If none match, return `uncaught`.
constraints: Subclass before base is the useful order
hints: A handler matches the raised type or one of its bases from the chain above.
Return the first match. Do not prefer a more specific later handler.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: except clauses are tried in source order, and a base class earlier than a subclass makes the subclass clause dead.

editorial: except clauses are tried in source order, and a base class earlier than a subclass makes the subclass clause dead. This function is that scan. The inheritance you need is only the small chain in the statement, not a full MRO of the interpreter.
